A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same sinusoidal-network initialization and frequency-bounding work despite the changed title and TUNER name. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-reconstruction experiments, signal and gradient PSNR measurements, initialization and bounding ablations, and comparisons with SIREN and BACON.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and reports additional comparisons involving ReLU, FFM, and BANF, alongside spatial error maps.

M1.justification: The frozen integer input frequencies, low/high-frequency sampling, hidden-weight initialization, fixed clipping, and learnable tanh bounds with regularization are retained. TUNER names the existing approach; the explicit sampling proportion and relocated half-cube explanation do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Kodak image reconstruction and signal/gradient evaluation remain the principal coverage. v1's separate texture-periodicity comparison against SIREN, using an image attributed to Cimpoi et al. in Section 4.1, disappears. The Kodak sub-periodicity examples remain, and the new comparisons introduce no additional application domain.

E2.justification: v2 Figure 1 adds evaluated ReLU and Fourier feature mapping (FFM) comparators, and Figure 13 adds BANF to bandlimit comparisons. SIREN and BACON remain, substantially broadening the actual comparator set beyond v1.

E3.justification: New comparisons specify matched model sizes/training conditions and a roughly 67K-parameter BACON/BANF/TUNER comparison at b=60/130 with common spectrum computation. Reported ablation settings also change: b=16 to 43 in v1 Figure 3a/v2 Figure 5, b=34 to 41 for learned bounds, and odd to even frequencies in the supplementary sub-periodicity example. The latter two reuse their plots, so these revisions do not establish reruns. The main 90/10 split and PSNR protocol remain.

E4.justification: v2 adds spatial error analysis comparing SIREN and TUNER in supplementary Section 2.4 and extends the bandlimit/artifact study with BANF. Initialization illustrations are revised, while the texture-periodicity demonstration is removed. Most existing ablations, including half-cube sampling, fixed/learned bounds, and layer composition, are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same image-level PSNR mean/standard-deviation reporting and shaded half-cube comparison curves. No new repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are reported.

E6.justification: v2 adds ReLU/FFM reconstruction and convergence results, BANF artifact findings, and spatial error maps, and replaces some initialization examples. Tables 1–2 are unchanged; Table 3 edits SIREN's test-signal PSNR at b=171, m=n=416 from 26.79 to 26.7. The stability caption changes from m<n to m>n in v1 Figure 11/v2 Figure 12. The relocated depth and original BACON results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v1 Appendix D works through two hidden layers and states that further generalization is analogous; v2 supplementary Section 1.2 formalizes that extension as arbitrary-depth Theorem 3 with an inductive proof. Section 1.1 also restores the missing 1/pi normalization in the Bessel definition and corrects a sine-to-cosine error in the proof. The core expansion and amplitude-bound theorems remain unchanged.

C1.justification: v2's abstract and contribution list explicitly claim faster, more stable training than previous approaches and prevention of overfitting, broadening the comparative contribution beyond v1's emphasis on spectral analysis and control mechanisms. The central expansion, initialization, and bounding contributions remain the same.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new error maps as evidence that SIREN's high-frequency fitting produces noise in low-detail regions, while TUNER accommodates regional spectral content. It adds discussion of BANF filtering artifacts and revises the learned-bound interpretation. The limitations concerning image-only experiments and predominantly single-hidden-layer architectures remain.

D1.justification: v2 documents the 70% low-frequency sampling proportion, additional architecture/epoch settings, and details of the retained layer-composition experiment, and adds a Kodak dataset URL. It removes v1's statement that the implementation is based on the MRNet repository. Adam, the learning rate, and GPU information remain; many additions disclose existing settings rather than demonstrate experimental changes.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations including FRESH, FINER, WIRE, SPDER, and BANF, with substantive positioning against BANF's grid-based frequency control. The Smith-normal-form reference changes from Mordell to Zippel, and the texture reference disappears. Most existing related-work discussion and theoretical positioning are retained.

P1.justification: The title, author/affiliation information, abstract, introduction, and substantial portions of the method narrative are rewritten, with TUNER terminology introduced throughout. The appendices are reorganized into a separately titled supplement with contents and grouped theory/experiment sections; several explanations and experiments move between the main text and supplement.

P2.justification: The main text changes from one to two columns and adds a results teaser, method schematic, BANF comparison, and spatial error visualization. Initialization displays are redesigned, while the original depth and BACON figures move to the supplement. Tables are compressed, with Table 3 adding boldface performance highlighting.

improvement.justification: The explicit general-depth proof and Bessel-formula corrections improve theoretical verifiability, while the controlled BANF comparison and spatial error maps strengthen empirical support. The overview diagram also clarifies the method. These are useful, bounded gains to a largely retained scientific study; the cramped Table 3 and removal of the texture demonstration and implementation-provenance statement modestly offset them.
